newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state seeks Banerj court order repeal.
newsitem.headline: Rio state seeks Banerj court order repeal.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state government is seeking to have a court injunction lifted which prevented its state bank Banerj from going on sale Tuesday as scheduled, Rio's Planning office said.
In a official statement sent to the press, the Planning Secretariat said the government was taking all measures so that the sell-off might take place.

Late Monday, Rio officials said Banerj's privatization auction, scheduled for today at 0900 local/1100 GMT, was postponed following a court injunction granted to the Association of Banerj's Employees who requested the suspension of the sale.

According to the statement, the auction was delayed indefinitely after judge Luiz Felipe da Silva Haddad ordered that the results of the auction would not be valid before the court issued a final ruling on the matter.
"The state's Privatization Committee found that these conditions would not give investors and Rio de Janeiro state the necessary safety (to allow the auction to take place)," the statement said.
Banerj bank and its insurer Banerj Seguros were due to be auctioned off for a total minimum price of 480 million reais on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
Banerj's privatization was to be the first of any Brazilian state bank.
-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 55-21-5074151
